title: On-chip Isotachophoresis for Separation of Ions and Purification of Nucleic Acids
protocol: Fill the North, East, and South reservoirs with 10-20 μL of 10% bleach.
Apply vacuum at the West reservoir for 2 min.
Empty the reservoirs.
Rinse the channel with 1 M sodium hydroxide for 2 min.
Empty the reservoirs.
Clean the channel with de-ionized water (DI).
Rinse the channel with LE for ~2 min.
Prepare 1 mL of LE consisting of 100 mM HCl, 200 mM tris, and 1% PVP.
Prepare 1 mL TE consisting of 100 mM HEPES and 200 mM tris.
Combine 90 μl of TE with 10 μl of 1 μM Alexa Fluor 488 (AF488).
Rinse the West reservoir with LE as described in Part 2.
Empty the West reservoir and clean it a few times with DI to dilute any remaining LE.
Fill the West reservoir with 20 μL TE containing AF488.
Place the positive electrode in the East reservoir and the ground (negative) electrode in the West reservoir.
Apply 2 μA (constant current).
Monitor the sample peak migrating from the West reservoir to the East reservoir.
Obtain a sample of E. coli cells to a density greater than 108 CFU/mL.
Transfer 1 mL cell culture into a microcentrifuge tube and pellet by centrifugation at 4000g for 6 min.
Re-suspend the pellet in 80 μL RNase-free water.
Add 10 μL of lysing agent to the re-suspended cells.
Mix gently and incubate for 5 mins. at room temperature.
Add 10 μL of 1 M sodium hydroxide to raise the lysate pH to ~12.5.
Gently actuate the pipette up and down until the solution becomes clear.
Combine 10 μL of lysate with 90 μL of 50 mM tricine and 100 mM bis-tris.
Prepare 1 mL of LE consisting of 500 mM bis-tris, 250 mM HCl, 1% PVP, and 1X SYBR Green II.
Fill the microfluidic chip with LE as described in Part 3.
Replace the contents of the East reservoir with PCR-compatible LE containing 50mM bis-tris, 25 mM HCl, and 0.1% PVP for off-chip analysis.
Apply 1000 V between the East and West wells to begin the experiment.
At the end of the experiment, mix the reservoir contents by repeated pipetting.
Extract a 5 μL volume for analysis by quantitative RT-PCR.
Prepare 1 mL LE consisting of 100 mM ethanolamine, 200 mM tricine, and 1% PVP, and 100 μM Rhodamine 6G.
Prepare 1 mL TE consisting of 20 mM tris, 40 mM tricine.
Mix 90 μL of TE with 10 μL each of 50 mM arginine and 50 mM lysine to prepare the sample.
Dispense 20 μL LE in the West and North reservoirs.
Dispense the prepared sample in the East reservoir.
Apply vacuum at South reservoir for 1 min.
Rinse the East well with DI and replace with TE (TE without sample).
Apply 500 V between the East and West reservoirs.
Dilute sample ions focus in "peak mode" ITP.
Mix two distinct dilute species with the LE and TE zones for peak mode focusing.
The electric field is determined solely by the LE and TE, not the sample species.
Sample ions are mixed with TE in a semi-infinite injection.
Focus sample ions together at the ITP interface in a roughly Gaussian peak.
Focusing criterion applies to strongly ionized species.
Conduct experiments showing Alexa Fluor 488 focused in peak mode for various applied currents.
Observe that the sample peak width is inversely proportional to current.
The self-sharpening interface resists dispersion due to pressure-driven flow.
Reconstitute E. coli cell culture nucleic acid using lysozyme-assisted alkaline lysing.
Purify nucleic acid from the lysate using selective electrophoretic focusing via ITP.
Mix TE buffer with the lysate containing target nucleic acid, proteins, and PCR inhibitors.
Select appropriate trailing and leading ions to enable selective focusing of target nucleic acid.
Collect purified genetic material after ITP purification.
Perform qRT-PCR analyses on the extracted genetic material using Power SYBR Green RNA-to-CT 1-Step Kit.
Use forward primer (5'-CGGATTGGAGTCTGCAACTCG) and reverse primer (5'-CACAAAGTGGTAAGCGCCCTC) at a concentration of 150 nM each.
Conduct qRT-PCR using recommended thermal cycling conditions.
